174	## 4. Derivation Chains
175	
176	Show how the ground truths combine into conclusions. Every conclusion offered in this analysis must have exactly one chain here — no more (no redundant restatement), no fewer (no orphaned conclusions).
177	
178	**Chain numbering convention.** Number each `### Conclusion:` block in this section `C1`,
179	`C2`, ... in document order (e.g., `### Conclusion C1: [Conclusion text]`). The §6→§4
180	closure ledger (the agent body — `SKILL.md` on the skill surface, `agents/first-principles.md` on the agent surface — "Before presenting conclusions") cites these IDs when mapping a
181	Conclusion-section (section 6) claim back to the chain in this section that established it.
182	
183	**Chain format:**
184	
185	```text
186	GT-N + GT-M → [intermediate claim] → [conclusion]
187	```
188	
189	The one-line form is the degenerate case, used only when the whole chain fits on one physical line; a chain that does not fit uses the head-plus-arrow-led form, and a hop is split rather than continued on a second line.
190	
191	Each chain must contain at least one intermediate step. A chain that goes directly from its head inputs to conclusion is incomplete — the intermediate is where the reasoning happens. The intermediate must be a new claim that could not be stated from any single head input alone. If no intermediate can be stated, the conclusion is either a restatement of a head input (trivial) or a reasoning step is missing.
192	
193	**No-wrap rule.** A hop occupies exactly one physical line. Every line after the head begins with `→` and carries exactly one complete hop; a hop is never broken across physical lines. A chain needing more hops continues on further arrow-led lines. A hop too long for comfort is SPLIT, not wrapped — the analysis renders as Markdown, so a long hop soft-wraps for the reader without breaking the form.
194	
195	```text
196	GT-1 ([brief fact label]) + GT-6 ([brief fact label])
197	→ [intermediate claim]
198	→ [further intermediate]
199	→ [conclusion]
200	```
201	
202	**Head-input rule.** The head line lists the inputs the chain consumes: each is a `GT-N` identifier (`GT-N?` when the ground truth is unverified) or a `Cn` identifier, optionally followed by a parenthesized gloss, joined to the next by `+`. The first `→` closes the head. An input carrying unparenthesized prose — `C2's threshold` — is not an identifier and does not parse; write `C2 (threshold)` in every position. The mechanical form check detects that violation only when the prose input is the last one before the first `→`; in an earlier position the check matches the well-formed remainder and scores the head conforming, so the rule binds in positions the check does not reach.
203	
204	```text
205	GT-1? ([brief fact label]) + C2 ([brief fact label])
206	→ [intermediate claim]
207	→ [conclusion]
208	```
209	
210	The head grammar governs the head line only. A hop is prose: `C2's saving` is fine after the first `→`, and is not an input reference. One exception: a hop must not begin with a `GT-N` identifier, which the form check reads as the head of a new chain and which therefore ends this one — write `→ the duty cycle stated in GT-4 is the binding term`, not `→ GT-4's stated duty cycle is the binding term`. The form check detects that violation only while fewer than two hops precede it; in a later position the check matches the preceding hops and scores the chain conforming, so the rule binds in positions the check does not reach.
211	
212	The mechanical form check additionally rejects a chain whose head or first hop closes its own sentence before the next `→`: it reads the following arrow-led line as a new statement and ends the chain there, so a chain satisfying every rule above is scored malformed for that reason alone. The check reaches only that position — a hop that closes its own sentence from the second hop onward does not change the verdict — which is why intermediate hops carry no terminal punctuation in this project's worked examples.
213	
214	**Conforming — head, then one hop per line:**
215	
216	```text
217	GT-1 (Lambda $/GB-s, AWS pricing) + GT-6 (Fargate $/vCPU-hr, AWS pricing)
218	→ Lambda costs 2.10× per unit of actual compute
219	→ sustained workloads belong on Fargate
220	```
221	
222	**Non-conforming — a hop broken across physical lines:**
223	
224	```text
225	GT-1 (Lambda $/GB-s, AWS pricing) + GT-6 (Fargate $/vCPU-hr, AWS pricing)
226	→ Lambda costs 2.10× per unit of actual compute
227	  once idle-time billing is included
228	→ sustained workloads belong on Fargate
229	```
230	
231	The continuation line does not begin with `→`, so the chain terminates at the head's first hop and what remains reads as an incomplete chain.
232	
233	**Non-conforming — the same hops rendered as a numbered list:**
234	
235	```text
236	1. GT-1 (Lambda $/GB-s, AWS pricing) + GT-6 (Fargate $/vCPU-hr, AWS pricing)
237	2. Lambda costs 2.10× per unit of actual compute
238	3. sustained workloads belong on Fargate
239	```
240	
241	A numbered list restates each hop as its own GT-headed one-hop chain, which reads as several incomplete chains rather than one complete one — the intermediate steps stop being connected to the conclusion they build toward.
242	
243	**Non-conforming — an input carrying unparenthesized prose:**
244	
245	```text
246	GT-13? (bill composition unknown) + GT-12? (duty cycle unknown) + C2's threshold
247	→ target quantity: fraction of total AWS bill removed by the migration
248	→ the bracket straddles zero, so its two ends recommend opposite actions
249	```
250	
251	`C2's threshold` is not an identifier — it is a possessive prose phrase — so the head does not parse; the third input must be written `C2 (threshold)`.
252	
253	**Conforming — the same head with the upstream chain as an input:**
254	
255	```text
256	GT-13? (bill composition unknown) + GT-12? (duty cycle unknown) + C2 (threshold)
257	→ target quantity: fraction of total AWS bill removed by the migration
258	→ the bracket straddles zero, so its two ends recommend opposite actions
259	```
260	
261	Exactly one token differs from the block above: a `Cn` identifier with a parenthesized gloss is an admissible head input, on equal footing with a `GT-N` identifier.
262	
263	**Conforming — a chain consuming only upstream conclusions:**
264	
265	```text
266	C1 (2.20× at full duty) + C2 (conditional on an unmeasured threshold) + C4 (unconditional, zero code change) + C5 (~73% ceiling, no execution-model change)
267	→ C4 and C5 deliver verified savings that do not depend on any property of your workload
268	→ C2's saving depends entirely on a duty-cycle figure nobody has measured
269	```
270	
271	A head may consist entirely of `Cn` inputs with no `GT-N` term. The second hop's `C2's saving` is prose, not a head input — the head-only scope note is what permits it here.
272	
273	**Non-conforming, and undetected by the form check — the same prose input in a non-final position:**
274	
275	```text
276	GT-13? (bill composition unknown) + C2's threshold + GT-12? (duty cycle unknown)
277	→ target quantity: fraction of total AWS bill removed by the migration
278	→ the bracket straddles zero, so its two ends recommend opposite actions
279	```
280	
281	This head breaks the same rule as the non-conforming block above and is equally non-conforming, but the mechanical form check scores it conforming — with a well-formed input still to its right the check matches from `GT-12?` onward and never reaches `C2's threshold`. Write `C2 (threshold)` wherever the input sits; the rule is the contract, and the check is a partial instrument for it.
282	
283	**Non-conforming — a hop beginning with a GT-N identifier:**
284	
285	```text
286	C1 (2.20× at full duty) + C2 (conditional on an unmeasured threshold)
287	→ GT-4's stated duty cycle is the binding term in both estimates
288	→ the bracket straddles zero, so its two ends recommend opposite actions
289	```
290	
291	The second line reads as the head of a new chain because it begins with a `GT-N` identifier, so this chain ends after its head and what remains is an incomplete chain — the possessive is not the problem, the leading identifier is.
292	
293	**Conforming — the same hop with the identifier moved off the front:**
294	
295	```text
296	C1 (2.20× at full duty) + C2 (conditional on an unmeasured threshold)
297	→ the duty cycle stated in GT-4 is the binding term in both estimates
298	→ the bracket straddles zero, so its two ends recommend opposite actions
299	```
300	
301	Exactly one clause is reordered and the chain is whole again; naming a ground truth inside a hop is fine, leading with its identifier is not.
302	
303	**Non-conforming, and undetected by the form check — the GT-led hop in a later position:**
304	
305	```text
306	C1 (2.20× at full duty) + C2 (conditional on an unmeasured threshold)
307	→ the bracket straddles zero, so its two ends recommend opposite actions
308	→ the second reading is the binding one
309	→ GT-4's stated duty cycle is the binding term in both estimates
310	```
311	
312	This hop breaks the same rule as the non-conforming block above and is equally non-conforming, but the mechanical form check scores it conforming — the check has already satisfied its two-arrow requirement on the hops that precede it, so the leading identifier ends the chain there without changing the verdict. Write `→ the duty cycle stated in GT-4 is the binding term in both estimates` wherever the hop sits; the rule is the contract, and the check is a partial instrument for it.
313	
314	**Non-conforming — the first hop closing its own sentence:**
315	
316	```text
317	C1 (2.20× at full duty) + C2 (conditional on an unmeasured threshold)
318	→ C1's saving is unconditional and does not depend on workload shape.
319	→ C2's saving is real only above the duty-cycle threshold this estimate assumes
320	```
321	
322	This chain violates none of R1-R9 — every input parses, every hop states one inference, no hop leads with a `GT-N` identifier — and is scored malformed anyway, because the mechanical form check ends the chain the moment the first hop closes its own sentence, before its two-arrow requirement is satisfied, and never reaches the well-formed hop that follows.
323	
324	**Conforming — the same chain with the first hop's terminal period removed:**
325	
326	```text
327	C1 (2.20× at full duty) + C2 (conditional on an unmeasured threshold)
328	→ C1's saving is unconditional and does not depend on workload shape
329	→ C2's saving is real only above the duty-cycle threshold this estimate assumes
330	```
331	
332	Exactly one character differs from the block above: the terminal period. Removing it, and nothing else, restores the two-arrow match the check requires.
333	
334	**Non-conforming, and undetected by the form check — the same period moved to a later hop:**
335	
336	```text
337	C1 (2.20× at full duty) + C2 (conditional on an unmeasured threshold)
338	→ C1's saving is unconditional and does not depend on workload shape
339	→ the migration case does not rest on C1 alone
340	→ C2's saving is real only above the duty-cycle threshold this estimate assumes.
341	```
342	
343	This block breaks the identical rule one hop later and is equally non-conforming, but the mechanical form check scores it conforming — with two hops already matched before the closing sentence is reached, the check has satisfied its two-arrow requirement and the sentence-closing period on the third hop has no following line left to block. Write the closing hop with no terminal punctuation wherever it sits; the rule is the contract, and the check is a partial instrument for it.
344	
345	**One-inference rule.** A hop states exactly ONE inference. If a hop joins two claims with "and", or carries a parenthetical that could stand as its own claim, it is two hops — split it.
346	
347	TELL (not the rule): a hop past ~200 characters is almost always two hops. Measure the hop, then split — do not wrap it, and do not trim words to hit a number.
348	
349	Inline annotations (`*[Assumes: A14 — …]*`) attach to the end of the hop line they qualify and do not start a new hop.
350	
351	### Converting structured-technique outputs into chains
352	
353	Structured-technique outputs (trade-off matrices, second-order effect lists) do not appear in this section as-is — each converts into the chain format above using the rule for its technique below. This subsection is the single source of truth for the conversion; the per-technique Handoff sections point back here rather than restating it, so future structured techniques extend this one place.
354	
355	**Trade-off matrix → one chain.** A trade-off matrix collapses into ONE chain whose intermediate cites the winning weighted total and whose endpoint names a single recommended option:
356	
357	```text
358	GT-refs (criteria's factual basis) → weighted totals (the winning total vs. the runner-up, naming the high-weight criteria that drive it) → recommended option
359	```
360	
361	Example: `GT-2 + GT-5 (criteria facts) → weighted totals: B=82 > A=64, driven by reliability×warranty → recommend B`. The full matrix stays in the technique's own output — this subsection carries only the single collapsed chain, never the matrix re-expressed row-by-row (that would violate the one-chain-per-conclusion rule above). An exact tie between weighted totals still resolves to a single named recommended option; a tie must not produce a multi-option chain endpoint. **Exact-tie tiebreak (deterministic):** on an exact tie, prefer the option with fewer `GT-N?` (unverified) inputs among its winning criteria; if still tied, name both totals in the chain intermediate but select the first-listed option as the chain endpoint, and flag the tie explicitly in the Conclusion section's confidence line.
362	
363	**Second-order effect list → order-marked extension.** A second-order effect list extends the parent chain IN PLACE as additional order-marked steps, each carrying the same evidentiary discipline as the first-order steps that produced the conclusion:
364	
365	```text
366	GT-N → first-order conclusion →[2nd] [2nd-order effect] →[3rd] [3rd-order effect] (contradicts GT-M → back to Phase 2)
367	```
368	
369	Example: `GT-1 → first-order conclusion →[2nd] flag-config surface grows →[3rd] flag debt accumulates (contradicts GT-4 → back to P2)`. The order marks (`[2nd]`, `[3rd]`) make the extension's sequence legible. A contradicting effect routes the conclusion back to Phase 2 — never directly to Phase 3 or past Phase 2. A pass that surfaces no non-contradicting downstream effect leaves the parent chain unextended — a clean no-op, not an error.
370	
371	### Confidence levels, defined
372	
373	`HIGH`, `MEDIUM` and `LOW` name how much of a chain is **outstanding** — not how strongly the analysis believes its conclusion. Three axes decide the band, each answerable by inspecting what the chain already carries on the page:
374	
375	- **Inputs** — the provenance of every identifier on the head line: an unsuffixed `GT-N` with a named read-at-source location, a `?`-marked ground truth, or a `Cn` carrying its own band.
376	- **Inference** — whether each hop the chain's endpoint depends on follows from the line above it, or needs a premise supplied by an `[Assumes: A-N]` annotation.
377	- **Rivals** — whether a competing conclusion from the same ground truths survives, and what rules it out. Section 5 is where the ruling-out is written down, so a chain answers this axis by pointing at its own Abandoned Reasoning entry as readily as by carrying the rival on its confidence line.
378	
379	**The band is the lowest the three axes license.** A chain is not HIGH because two of them are clean.
380	
381	**HIGH — nothing on this chain is outstanding.** Every identifier on the head line is an unsuffixed `GT-N` whose read-at-source location is named, or a `Cn` itself rated HIGH; every hop the endpoint depends on follows from the line above it by deduction, by arithmetic that recomputes when redone independently of the chain text, or by a regularity cited to an unsuffixed ground truth; and the strongest rival conclusion the analysis considered is named — on this confidence line or in a section 5 entry this chain points to — together with the ground truth or chain that rules it out, that ruling-out input itself unsuffixed. A chain whose endpoint a live alternative still contests is unexamined, not certain: it is MEDIUM at best.
382	
383	An `[Assumes: A-N]` annotation on a hop shorts the Inference axis **unless** the confidence line says what becomes of the endpoint when that assumption fails and the endpoint still stands — *"A2 is that the CDN'd assets are versioned; if they were not, the CDN result would be weaker evidence still, so the conclusion is unaffected"*. An annotation on a hop that only qualifies a second-order extension, and not the endpoint, is outside this axis and the chain says which case it is. Stating the sensitivity is the work; an unexamined assumption is not the same thing as one whose falsity has been priced.
384	
385	The Rivals axis is answered when a section 5 entry names a competing conclusion to this chain's endpoint and the chain or ground truth that ruled it out, or when the endpoint is itself a ruling-out — a chain establishing that some option does not work has already done the rival's work and does not need a rival of its own. It is short when a competing conclusion has been raised anywhere in the analysis and nothing settles it, and when the analysis reaches a positive recommendation with no section 5 content bearing on it at all.
386	
387	**MEDIUM — exactly one axis is short, and the shortfall is named and bounded.** One of: an identifier on the head line is `?`-marked or is a `Cn` rated MEDIUM; or at most one hop the endpoint depends on rests on a stated `[Assumes: A-N]` premise whose failure the chain has not priced; or a rival to the endpoint is live and nothing in the analysis settles it. The confidence line names which axis is short, names the specific input, hop or rival, and states what would close it — the verification that would remove an input as a cause of the downgrade, the evidence that would establish an assumed premise, or the observation that would settle between this conclusion and its rival. A MEDIUM chain is one whose weakness a reader can point at.
388	
389	**LOW — the shortfall is unbounded, or more than one axis is short.** Two or more axes short at once; or an input is `?` with no verification path available; or a hop's missing premise cannot be stated as an assumption at all, so the analysis cannot say what would make the step valid; or a rival survives that no available observation would settle. A LOW chain is reportable, and a conclusion resting on it alone is not actionable.
390	
391	**Calibration rule.** Each rating is the highest its inputs, hops and rivals license, **and no higher**. Rating above what the axes license over-claims. Rating below it is a defect of the same kind: a chain meeting HIGH on all three axes and written MEDIUM misreports the analysis's own strength, and a document whose every chain carries the same defensive band tells a reader nothing about which parts to trust. Criterion 5 scores calibration, not altitude — an analysis whose every band is the one its axes license is Rigorous whether its conclusion is HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW.
392	
393	**The caps are consequences, not extra rules.** The unverified-input rule (D-07) below and the ceiling at the lowest-rated chain a head cites are what the Inputs axis says, restated for the two cases that occur most often; they are the fast check, and these definitions are what they check for. A cap never licenses a band on its own — it bounds from above, and the band is still the lowest any of the three axes licenses.
394	
395	**Confidence pre-check (Inputs axis).** Directly above every `**Confidence:**` line — each §4 chain's and the §6 Conclusion's — write one `**Pre-check:**` line, with nothing between it and the `**Confidence:**` line it checks:
396	
397	```text
398	**Pre-check:** head GT-1, GT-3?, C2 (MEDIUM) · ?-marked: GT-3? · lowest cited: MEDIUM · Inputs ceiling: MEDIUM
399	**Confidence:** MEDIUM — GT-3? is unverified; …
400	```
401	
402	Four fields, separated by ` · `: `head` lists every identifier on the chain's head line (the part before the first `→`), in order, comma-separated, a `?` suffix kept (`GT-3?`), each `Cn` followed by its own stated band in parentheses (`C2 (MEDIUM)`) — for the §6 roll-up, `head` is every chain the Conclusion rests on, each with its band, plus any `GT-N?` the Conclusion rests on directly. `?-marked` lists the `?`-suffixed identifiers from `head`, comma-separated, or the token `none`. `lowest cited` is the lowest band among the `Cn` in `head`, or `none` when `head` cites no chain. `Inputs ceiling` is the Inputs axis's bound: `LOW` if `lowest cited` is LOW; otherwise `MEDIUM` if `?-marked` is not `none` or `lowest cited` is MEDIUM; otherwise `HIGH`.
403	
404	This is the Inputs axis of "Confidence levels, defined" made procedural — Inference and Rivals are not scored on this line, and can only lower the band further. The ceiling bounds from above, as the caps-are-consequences paragraph above states; the `**Confidence:**` label may equal it or sit below it, and never above it — a below-ceiling label is explained by the Confidence line itself, not by the pre-check. In §6, the pre-check line is itself a Conclusion-section claim under the Claim inventory rule below, and it is cited by the chains its own `head` names.
405	
406	### Conclusion C1: [Conclusion text]
407	
408	GT-N ([brief fact label, source]) + GT-M ([brief fact label, source])
409	→ [intermediate claim — a new inference statable from combining GT-N and GT-M but from neither alone]

416	**Unverified input rule (D-07):** A chain that includes any `GT-N?` input must end with a MEDIUM or LOW confidence line. This is a ceiling: it bounds the rating from above and is never a reason to rate a chain HIGH, and a cited chain rated MEDIUM under a validation-rubric EXCEPT clause still caps every chain that cites it. Every MEDIUM or LOW confidence line explains only its own chain's rating, so its validity never depends on how far away a cap originates. The line names each `GT-N?` input with the verification that would remove it as a cause of the downgrade. It names each `Cn` on the chain's head rated below HIGH and need not re-explain that `Cn`, whose own confidence line carries the explanation, so no line has to trace a cited chain's lineage. A MEDIUM or LOW conclusion without this explanation does not satisfy D-07.
454	
455	**Claim inventory.** A Conclusion-section claim is a bold lead-in whose colon closes the bold span, or a numbered or bulleted list item, and the four lead-ins this template prescribes — `**Recommended approach:**`, `**Key insight:**`, `**Trade-offs acknowledged:**` and `**Confidence:**` — are always claims and each must cite a chain; the `**Confidence:**` line discharges that obligation through the chains D-07 already requires it to name, and a HIGH line whose justification prose names no chain is the one position where this rule and the extractor can disagree, so name the chain there too; nothing inside a fenced block is ever a claim whatever its shape, a near-paraphrase restatement or direct entailment of an already-cited claim earlier in the same section is not a second claim, and prose carrying neither a bold colon lead-in nor a list marker is not a claim at all. 501	```

## 4. Derivation Chains

### C1 — What job would a free tier actually do here?

```text
GT-2 (outbound+referral only, no inbound channel) + GT-6 (revenue impact ≈ N × r × LTV)
→ a free tier's revenue contribution requires nonzero top-of-funnel signup volume N
→ that signup volume is currently ≈0 per GT-2, because no mechanism routes visitors to a signup page at any volume
→ therefore a free tier cannot presently function as a distribution/acquisition mechanism for this company — it has nothing to convert
→ its only remaining candidate jobs are competitive-parity signaling (addressed in C3) or a PLG motion that would first require building the missing inbound engine (A-2), which is a separate, larger project than "add a free tier"
```
**Pre-check:** head = GT-2 (unsuffixed) · GT-6 (unsuffixed) · ?-marked = none · lowest cited = none · Inputs ceiling = HIGH
**Confidence: HIGH.** Inputs are both unsuffixed ground truths; inference is a direct application of a definitional identity (GT-6) to a stipulated fact (GT-2); no live rival reading of this specific chain — the only way N is nonzero today is referral traffic landing on a public signup page, which GT-2 says does not exist as a channel.

### C2 — Cost/NPV model: what has to be true for a free tier to be NPV-positive

```text
GT-3 (cost scales with active users, not payers) + GT-7? (cost/active-free-user, $50–500/yr, mid $200) + GT-8? (avg. 1.5 yr tenure as free before converting/churning) + GT-9? (LTV of a converted customer, $9K–24K, mid $15K)
→ a free tier carries a guaranteed, non-zero cost for every active free user regardless of conversion
→ breakeven free-to-paid conversion rate r* solves N·r·LTV = N·c·t, and N cancels out of the equation entirely
→ r* = (c × t) / LTV — breakeven conversion rate depends only on cost-per-user, tenure, and converted LTV, not on funnel volume
→ at central estimates, r* = ($200 × 1.5) / $15,000 ≈ 2.0%; at the pessimistic-cost end, r* = ($500 × 1.5) / $9,000 ≈ 8.3%; at the optimistic-cost end, r* = ($50 × 1.5) / $24,000 ≈ 0.3%
→ 2% sits inside the range typically cited for B2B self-serve freemium conversion (roughly 1–5%), so the unit economics are plausible but not safely so — the breakeven rate is highly sensitive to the GT-7?/GT-8?/GT-9? estimate brackets, none of which this company has measured directly [Assumes: A-10]
```
**Pre-check:** head = GT-3 (unsuffixed) · GT-7? · GT-8? · GT-9? (all `?`) · ?-marked = GT-7, GT-8, GT-9 · lowest cited = none (no chains cited) · Inputs ceiling = MEDIUM
**Confidence: MEDIUM.** Would be HIGH if the Inputs axis weren't carrying three `?`-marked estimate inputs; the arithmetic identity (Inference axis) is sound and not in dispute. What would remove the cap: replacing GT-7?/GT-8?/GT-9? with this company's own measured figures from a pilot (chain C5) — that is precisely the "no pilot data" gap named in GT-4, and it is the single biggest lever on this chain's confidence. **Key structural insight (independent of the exact bracket): breakeven viability does not depend on funnel volume N — it depends only on cost-per-user, tenure, and converted LTV.** This matters for C1: even if C1's funnel problem were solved tomorrow, C2's unit economics would still need to clear ~2–8% conversion before volume helps rather than hurts.

### C3 — Is "competitors all have a free tier" real evidence of necessity?

```text
GT-5 (all named competitors have a free tier)
→ the competitor set was selected because they compete in this category — a free tier may be structural to their own (possibly lower-ACV, higher-volume, self-serve) GTM motion rather than evidence that any GTM motion needs one
→ no win/loss data is cited showing a lost deal where the prospect named "no free tier" as the reason
→ therefore GT-5 is weak evidence for this company's specific question and is better read as a mimicry/survivorship signal than a demand signal
```
**Pre-check:** head = GT-5 (unsuffixed) · ?-marked on head = none · dependency note: Inference rests on [Assumes: A-3?], an unverified assumption not itself a head identifier · lowest cited = none · Inputs ceiling = HIGH on Inputs alone, held to MEDIUM by the Inference axis per A-3?
**Confidence: MEDIUM.** The logical critique of the parity argument is sound (Inference axis is clean), but the chain cannot rule out that *some* lost deals genuinely did hinge on "try before you buy" friction — that would require win/loss interview data this company does not currently collect on this question. What would raise this to HIGH: running a lightweight win/loss review on the next 10–20 closed-lost outbound deals, explicitly asking whether a free/trial option would have changed the outcome.

### C4 — Second-order sales-motion risk (actor lens + time lens)

```text
GT-2 (consultative outbound motion, no existing self-serve exit ramp)
→ [Assumes: A-5] introducing any free/self-serve option gives an active-pipeline prospect a lower-commitment alternative to a signed $10K/yr contract
→ actor lens: sales reps may lean on "just try the free tier" to avoid a hard close conversation, shifting their own behavior away from the quota-driving motion that built GT-1's $2.4M ARR; procurement-side buyers may stall a decision pending self-service evaluation, lengthening cycle time
→ time lens: in the first 1–2 quarters this shows up as minor friction; if unmanaged for a year or more it can quietly re-shape the GTM motion into a hybrid the sales org was never comped or structured for (an org-design second-order effect, not just a revenue one) [Assumes: A-11]
→ this risk is real but containable — it is a reason to bound any experiment (trial, not perpetual access) and to keep the sales team, not a public signup page, as the gatekeeper of who gets it (see C5/C6)
```
**Pre-check:** head = GT-2 (unsuffixed) · ?-marked on head = none · dependency note: Inference rests on [Assumes: A-5?, A-11?], both unverified and not head identifiers · lowest cited = none · Inputs ceiling = HIGH on Inputs alone, held to MEDIUM by the Inference axis per A-5?/A-11?
**Confidence: MEDIUM.** The mechanism is well-established in B2B SaaS generally (Inference axis reasonably strong) but its magnitude for *this* sales team and *this* buyer profile is unverified (A-5 is untested) — what would resolve it: measuring sales-cycle length and realized ACV for trial-attached deals vs. non-trial deals during the pilot in C5/C6, which is exactly the tripwire built into the pre-mortem (process output, Adversarial pass record).

### C5 — Trade-off analysis: cheapest way to get real signal

Four options scored against six weighted criteria (full table and flip test are process output in this run; the collapsed result is reported here per the output template's §4 conversion rule). Options: **A** status quo (no pilot, no free tier); **B** time-boxed full-feature trial attached to existing outbound/referral leads; **C** full self-serve freemium launch; **D** perpetual free tier scoped to a narrow, non-core ICP segment.

```text
GT-2 (no inbound channel, no self-serve infra) + GT-3 (cost scales with active users, open-ended exposure risk)
→ option C requires building the self-serve signup/metering/billing/upgrade infrastructure GT-2 confirms does not exist, and exposes GT-3's open-ended cost with the least-informative signal (volume will be near-zero anyway absent an inbound engine, and any data that does arrive conflates "no funnel" with "bad conversion economics")
→ option B reuses the existing outbound/referral funnel, bounds GT-3's cost exposure to a fixed trial window, and isolates the one unknown that actually matters here (GT-4's missing conversion rate) without also having to solve the funnel problem at the same time
→ weighted trade-off scoring (Signal quality, Build cost, Cost exposure, Sales-risk, Speed, Reversibility; weights 5/4/4/4/3/3) ranks B highest (102) ahead of A (83), D (61), C (34) [Assumes: A-12]
→ flip test: zeroing the single highest-leverage criterion for B (Signal quality, weight 5) still leaves B ahead of A by 4 points — no single-criterion weight change in the plausible range reverses the ranking; B is a robust choice, not a near-tie
→ therefore the cheapest path to real signal is a time-boxed trial attached to the existing sales motion, not a narrow-ICP pilot and not a full freemium launch
```
**Pre-check:** head = GT-2 (unsuffixed) · GT-3 (unsuffixed) · ?-marked = none on this chain's direct head (the trade-off's own inputs reuse GT-2/GT-3 directly; A-5/A-8 inform scoring rationale but are not head identifiers) · lowest cited = none · Inputs ceiling = HIGH
**Confidence: HIGH.** Inputs are unsuffixed ground truths; the trade-off procedure's weights were locked before scoring (per the procedure's discipline) and the flip test shows the ranking survives the largest plausible single-criterion perturbation. Rival considered and ruled out: "skip straight to full freemium because competitors already validated the model" — ruled out by C3 (competitor parity is weak evidence of transferability) and by C1 (the funnel precondition is absent regardless of what competitors validated elsewhere) — see §5 Abandoned Reasoning.

### C6 — Conditional recommendation with go/no-go thresholds

```text
C2 (breakeven r* ≈ 0.3–8.3%, central ≈2%, MEDIUM) + C5 (time-boxed trial is the robust choice, HIGH)
→ run a time-boxed (e.g., 30-day) full-feature trial attached to sales-qualified outbound/referral leads, not an open public signup
→ pre-commit, before launch, to explicit go/no-go thresholds derived from C2: proceed toward a broader/permanent free tier only if measured conversion r ≥ r* for the measured cost-per-active-trial-user, sustained across at least two cohorts
→ pre-mortem findings (process output, Adversarial pass record) attach four tripwires with named owners to this plan: decision-date discipline (Finance/exec), sales-cycle-length delta (Sales lead), cost-per-user overrun (Support/Ops lead), extension-request rate (Product/CS)
→ this converts GT-4's "no pilot data" gap into a bounded, owned, time-limited experiment rather than either an indefinite "no" or an uninstrumented "yes"
```
**Pre-check:** head = C2 (MEDIUM) · C5 (HIGH) · ?-marked = none directly on this chain's head (the `?` inputs are inherited through C2, already priced into C2's own band) · lowest cited = MEDIUM (C2) · Inputs ceiling = MEDIUM
**Confidence: MEDIUM**, capped by C2's MEDIUM (a chain is capped at the lowest-rated chain its head cites). What would remove the cap: the pilot itself (this chain's own recommendation) producing measured, company-specific values for GT-7?/GT-8?/GT-9?, at which point C2 — and therefore C6 — can be re-rated HIGH or re-rated down to a clear LOW/no-go, either of which is a strictly better state than today's unresolved MEDIUM.

## 5. Abandoned Reasoning

**What was tried:** Treat "skip the pilot and go straight to a full self-serve freemium launch, since every named competitor already validated the model" as the leading option.
**Why abandoned:** This conflates two distinct claims — "freemium works for category X" and "freemium works for *this company's* GTM motion." C1 shows the structural precondition (an inbound funnel to convert) is absent regardless of what competitors proved elsewhere; C3 shows the competitor-parity signal itself is weak (mimicry/survivorship, no win/loss evidence); C5's trade-off scoring ranks this option lowest of the four on signal quality, cost exposure, and reversibility (score 34 vs. 102 for the trial option).
**What it ruled out:** Full freemium launch (option C) as the near-term move; it remains a theoretically available later step only after the inbound-funnel precondition is separately solved and the pilot (C6) clears its thresholds.

**What was tried:** Treat the narrow-ICP perpetual free tier (option D — e.g., free for a non-core segment such as single-seat or hobbyist users) as a way to get real freemium signal without touching the core sales motion.
**Why abandoned:** It still requires building meaningful self-serve infrastructure (A-8 — this is not "just a pricing page"), carries GT-3's open-ended cost exposure (no time box), and the resulting conversion signal would come from a segment that is not the $10K-ACV buyer GT-1 is anchored to — so it answers a narrower, less decision-relevant question than C5's chosen option. Trade-off scoring (C5) ranked it third of four (61 vs. 102).
**What it ruled out:** A narrow-ICP permanent free tier as the *first* move; it remains a plausible *second* experiment if the core-motion trial (C6) succeeds and a genuinely distinct underserved segment is later identified.

**What was tried:** Treat "do nothing, indefinitely" (option A, status quo) as an acceptable permanent answer rather than a temporary default.
**Why abandoned:** Status quo scores well on every axis except the two that matter for resolving GT-4's actual gap — Signal quality and Speed to data (score 1 of 5 on each) — meaning it preserves optionality but never retires the uncertainty the user explicitly asked this analysis to address. C5's trade-off result (B beats A by 19 points, robust under the flip test) shows a bounded trial strictly dominates indefinite inaction once cost-exposure is controlled for.
**What it ruled out:** Permanent inaction as the final answer; it remains correct only as the fallback if C2's pessimistic-cost bracket is confirmed (see Section 6's flip condition for an outright "no").

## 6. Conclusion

**Recommended approach:** Do not launch a permanent or full self-serve free tier now. Instead, run a time-boxed (≈30-day) full-feature trial attached to sales-qualified outbound and referral leads — reusing the existing funnel rather than building a new one — with pre-committed go/no-go conversion and cost thresholds and four named, owned tripwires (decision-date discipline, sales-cycle-length delta, cost-per-user overrun, extension-request rate) (chain C6). Use the pilot's measured results to replace this analysis's estimated cost-model inputs (chain C2) with real numbers before deciding on anything broader.

**Key insight:** A free tier is a *conversion* mechanism, not a *demand-generation* mechanism — its revenue impact is the product of funnel volume, conversion rate, and converted LTV, and if funnel volume is zero the other two terms are irrelevant (chain C1). This company's GTM motion (outbound + referral, GT-2) currently supplies that volume at or near zero for a public free tier, which is why "add a free tier" is the wrong frame; "get a company-specific conversion-rate measurement cheaply, inside the motion that already works" (chain C5/C6) is the right one.

**Trade-offs acknowledged:** The recommended trial is not free of risk — it carries real, if bounded, sales-cycle-lengthening and cost-overrun exposure (chain C4), and it deliberately defers the two biggest upside scenarios (a real inbound/PLG motion, or full competitive parity) rather than capturing them immediately. It also does not resolve the "competitors all have one" perception question (chain C3) — a prospect who wants to self-serve evaluate today still cannot, during the trial design and rollout window.

**Pre-check:** head = C1 (HIGH) · C2 (MEDIUM) · C3 (MEDIUM) · C4 (MEDIUM) · C5 (HIGH) · C6 (MEDIUM) · GT-N? rested on directly = none beyond those already inside the cited chains · ?-marked = none new · lowest cited = MEDIUM · Inputs ceiling = MEDIUM
**Confidence: MEDIUM.** The structural argument against a full freemium launch today (C1, C5) is HIGH-confidence and not sensitive to the unresolved estimates. The conditional "run a trial, with these thresholds" recommendation is capped at MEDIUM by C2's unresolved cost/conversion brackets (GT-7?/GT-8?/GT-9?) and by C4's unverified cannibalization magnitude (A-5?) — both are exactly what the recommended trial (C6) is designed to resolve. Rivals: the strongest live rival — "skip the pilot, go straight to full freemium because competitors already proved it" — is ruled out in §5. No rival currently threatens the narrower claim that *some* instrumented, bounded experiment beats both permanent inaction and an uninstrumented full launch.

**Flip conditions:**
- **Flips to YES (broader/permanent free tier):** the pilot (C6) measures a sustained free-to-paid conversion rate at or above the breakeven r* implied by the *measured* (not estimated) cost-per-active-user and converted LTV, across at least two cohorts, **and** no material sales-cycle lengthening or realized-ACV erosion is observed (C4's risk does not materialize), **and** a genuine inbound-traffic source (content, SEO, community, partner-driven, or organic referral growth) exists or is concurrently built — because C1's volume term must be nonzero for any of this to matter at scale.
- **Flips to an outright NO, without even running the pilot:** Finance produces a measured (not estimated) cost-per-active-free-user high enough that the resulting breakeven r* exceeds realistic B2B self-serve conversion benchmarks (roughly >8–10%) even under optimistic LTV assumptions — in that case C2's economics fail regardless of execution quality, and the trial should not be run at all.
- **Default if neither flip condition is yet evaluated:** proceed with the bounded, instrumented trial in C6 — it is strictly better than guessing in either direction, and it is the cheapest available way to retire GT-4's "no pilot data" gap.

| A-1 | A free tier is primarily a distribution/acquisition mechanism (brings in new-to-company users who wouldn't otherwise be found) | convention | Challenge: does it hold without an inbound channel? | **Fails as stated for this company** — a free tier *converts* existing top-of-funnel traffic; it does not *generate* traffic. GT-2 confirms no inbound channel exists, so there is nothing for it to convert. | Verified by definitional reasoning, see GT-6 |

148	**Key insight:** A free tier is a *conversion* mechanism, not a *demand-generation* mechanism — its revenue impact is the product of funnel volume, conversion rate, and converted LTV, and if funnel volume is zero the other two terms are irrelevant (chain C1). content.text:
Stopping the file-formatting work as instructed. Here is the concise, decision-useful analysis directly.

## Ground truths (as given, with one important caveat)

- **GT-1**: $2.4M ARR, 240 paying teams, ~$10K average ACV.
- **GT-2**: 100% outbound + referral GTM; **no self-serve inbound channel exists today.**
- **GT-3**: Free-tier infra/support cost scales with *active* users, not paying users (Finance-confirmed) — a free tier is never literally free.
- **GT-4**: No historical free-to-paid conversion data exists; any conversion rate is speculative.
- **GT-5**: All named competitors have a free tier.

Caveat: these are the operator's own stipulated figures, not independently sourced by me (no CRM/Finance export opened) — treat them as solid in practice, but they are "stated," not "audited."

## Key challenged assumptions

| Assumption | Verdict |
|---|---|
| A free tier is a distribution/acquisition mechanism | **Discard** — a free tier *converts* existing top-of-funnel traffic; it doesn't generate it. With no inbound channel (GT-2), there's nothing to convert. |
| A free tier = a PLG motion that can bolt onto outbound | **Discard** — PLG needs self-serve signup infra *and* traffic feeding it; neither exists. This is a real build project, not a toggle. |
| "All competitors have one, so we need one" | **Challenge** — likely mimicry/survivorship. Competitors' free tiers are load-bearing to *different* (lower-ACV, higher-volume, self-serve) GTM motions. No win-loss data shows any deal was actually lost over this. |
| Free-tier converts will look like our $10K-ACV buyer | **Challenge** — self-selecting free signups in an outbound-qualified motion typically skew smaller/cheaper than the existing base. |
| A free tier will cannibalize outbound sales | **Challenge, plausible but unverified** — gives prospects a stalling/de-risking option; mechanism is well-known in B2B SaaS, magnitude here is unmeasured. |

## Cost-model logic (the core quantitative result)

Revenue impact of a free tier ≈ **N (signups) × r (conversion rate) × LTV (converted customer)**. If N ≈ 0 (true today, per GT-2), the other two terms don't matter — this is why "add a free tier" is the wrong frame for this company *right now*.

For the unit economics alone (ignoring N), breakeven conversion rate:
**r\* = (cost per active free user × avg. tenure as free) / LTV of a converted customer**

Using defensible brackets (cost $50–500/yr, mid $200; tenure 0.5–2.5yr, mid 1.5yr; converted LTV $9K–24K, discounted from the $10K ACV since free converts likely skew smaller, mid $15K):

- Central case: r\* ≈ **2.0%** — inside the typical 1–5% range cited for B2B self-serve freemium, so plausible but not safely so.
- Pessimistic cost case: r\* ≈ **8.3%** — above what's realistic.
- Optimistic cost case: r\* ≈ **0.3%** — trivially achievable.

**The breakeven math doesn't depend on funnel volume N at all** — only cost/user, tenure, and LTV. So volume determines how much is at stake, not whether the economics work. Since none of GT-7/8/9 (the cost, tenure, LTV inputs) have ever been measured by this company, this is the single biggest open question — bigger than the funnel problem, in terms of deciding "is this even viable."

## Second-order effects

- **Sales cannibalization**: a free/self-serve option gives active-pipeline prospects a lower-commitment alternative to a signed $10K contract; reps may lean on it as a crutch to avoid hard closes; procurement may use it to stall. Real risk, unverified magnitude.
- **Support load**: costs scale with active users (GT-3) — an unmetered, undifferentiated free cohort can blow past the cost-model's own assumptions and degrade support SLA for *paying* customers during any marketing-driven signup spike.
- **"Everyone else has one"**: weak evidence of necessity for this company specifically — it's evidence their free tier is structural to *their* (different) GTM motion, not evidence this company's outbound/referral motion needs one. No win-loss data ties any lost deal to this.

## Cheapest way to get real signal (before any full commitment)

Compared four options (full freemium launch / narrow-ICP perpetual free tier / time-boxed trial / status quo) on signal quality, build cost, cost exposure, sales-motion risk, speed, and reversibility: a **time-boxed (~30-day) full-feature trial attached to sales-qualified outbound/referral leads** dominates — it reuses the existing funnel (no new infra build), bounds cost exposure to a fixed window, and isolates the one unknown that matters (conversion rate) without also having to solve the funnel-building problem simultaneously. Going straight to full freemium conflates two different unknowns (does the product convert? does an inbound funnel even exist?) and get an ambiguous read on both for a much higher build cost and open-ended cost exposure.

Guardrails that matter if you run it: pre-commit go/no-go thresholds *before* launch (otherwise it drifts into a permanent unmanaged free tier with no decision ever made), meter/tag trial-user cost separately from day one, keep it sales-qualified rather than public self-serve, and track sales-cycle-length delta as a cannibalization tripwire.

## Recommendation and flip conditions

**Don't launch a permanent or full self-serve free tier now.** Run the time-boxed, sales-attached trial described above, with pre-committed thresholds, and use its *measured* results to replace the estimated cost-model inputs before deciding on anything broader. Confidence: **MEDIUM** — the "wrong frame" structural argument (no funnel to convert) is solid; the conditional trial recommendation is capped by the unmeasured cost/conversion brackets it's specifically designed to resolve.

- **Flips to YES** (broader/permanent free tier) if: the trial measures a sustained conversion rate ≥ the measured breakeven r\*, across ≥2 cohorts, **and** no material sales-cycle lengthening/ACV erosion shows up, **and** a real inbound-traffic source exists or is being built (volume still has to come from somewhere).
- **Flips to an outright NO** (skip even the trial) if: Finance's *measured* cost-per-active-free-user implies a breakeven r\* above ~8–10% — at that point the economics fail regardless of execution quality.
